rows.title: Gate-ROI Measurement Ledger — Prove What Each Gate Catches
rows.summary: OBJECTIVES' own 2026-06-09 stress-test note names 'gate-ROI unproven' as an open gap, yet no backlog item measures what the gates actually catch versus what they cost.
rows.cost_rationale: New parser over 185+ archived handoffs/verdicts plus report generation is a multi-file, >100k-token sweep.
rows.value_rationale: Advances O1/KR3 (gaps with impact rating) and O1/KR2: it closes the named 'gate-ROI unproven' gap with quantified evidence instead of assertion.
rows.deliverable: A gate-roi script under .tad/scripts/ plus .tad/evidence/research/gate-roi/gate-roi.csv and report.md showing, per Gate (1-4), P0/P1 catches, review rounds, and rework incidents extracted from archived HANDOFF/COMPLETION/verdict files — the dataset must cover at least 100 archived handoffs and every row must link to its source evidence file.

rows.title: Gate 3 hook args-shape bypass: malformed gate number silently passes
rows.summary: Independent defect found alongside the Gate 3 verdict-wording measurement: GATE_NUM is parsed with a line-start-anchored grep, so malformed args silently bypass the whole Gate 3 check block.
rows.cost_rationale: One parser in one hook plus regression tests; small, well-localised change.
rows.value_rationale: A silent fail-open in a gate hook defeats the review enforcement the whole TAD chain relies on.
rows.deliverable: Hook fix so GATE_NUM parsing rejects or correctly parses inputs like " 3" and "gate 3" instead of silently returning {} exit 0, with a regression test covering leading-space and word-form arguments, per HANDOFF-20260816-gate3-check8-audible.md §10.2(b).

rows.title: Release Full Version Sweep Gate — Prevent Historical Version Drift
rows.summary: Fix the adjacent-version-only release gate that permanently misses files stuck many versions behind (Alex SKILL.md was 18 versions stale).
rows.cost_rationale: One new mode in an existing script plus two advisory checks in the publish flow.
rows.value_rationale: Root-caused from a real release incident; once a file is missed it is missed forever under the current gate.
rows.deliverable: release-verify.sh `version-sweep` mode that regex-scans all version strings (excluding archive/evidence/CHANGELOG history and added_in/deprecated_in lines) and reports any not equal to $NEW, plus README What's New and GitHub repo-description freshness warnings in *publish.

rows.title: Local Wiki Build-Out to 30 Canon Sources
rows.summary: Local Wiki stands at 11 raw / 8 canon / 6 wiki pages against the >=30 source target; no backlog item grows the research knowledge base itself (Domain Pack Refresh covers tools/skills, not research sources).
rows.cost_rationale: Ingesting ~19 sources through the raw→canon→wiki pipeline is bulk content work, not a code change.
rows.value_rationale: Advances O3/KR1 directly: canon source count reaches the stated >=30 target from the current 8, restoring the KR the retired NotebookLM layer once satisfied.
rows.deliverable: research/ ingestion manifest plus at least 19 new sources processed raw→canon, bringing the Local Wiki canon count from 8 to >=30, with the FTS5 index rebuilt and a probe script demonstrating successful retrieval hits for 5 test queries recorded in research/evidence/.

rows.title: Capability-Acquisition Case Ledger — Evidence Behind the Differentiators
rows.summary: The 2026-06-09 stress-test falsified all 3 repositioning 'walls' as stated and left the differentiator 'rhetorical without evidence'; no backlog item builds the longitudinal case evidence for capability acquisition itself.
rows.cost_rationale: Evidence assembly across several real domain projects plus a synthesis rewrite of the positioning doc; 2-4 files but broad source gathering.
rows.value_rationale: Advances O1/KR2 directly: differentiators move from 3 rhetorical claims to >=3 evidence-backed ones, or are honestly downgraded — exactly the validation the KR demands.
rows.deliverable: .tad/evidence/capability-acquisition/cases.tsv with at least 6 completed real-domain cases (each row: domain, starting capability, ending capability, links to the artifacts/handoffs proving it) and an updated docs/value-proposition.md where each of the >=3 claimed differentiators carries at least 2 linked case evidences or is explicitly downgraded to unvalidated.

rows.title: skill-body-verify: SAFETY criterion from global count to line-set diff
rows.summary: Split-out small ticket (b) from the voided English-unification plan: the SAFETY check counts lines globally, so equal-count replacements of safety lines pass undetected today, independent of any translation work.
rows.cost_rationale: The line-set diff already exists in verify.sh's acref(); porting it is a focused two-file change with tests.
rows.value_rationale: A count-based safety check can be defeated by swapping safety lines one-for-one; line-set diffing closes a live hole in the SAFETY floor.
rows.deliverable: skill-body-verify.sh SAFETY criterion changed from the global SAFETY_FLOOR=70 count to a line-set diff reusing verify.sh's existing acref() implementation (bilingual, guards equal-count swaps), with a test showing an equal-count SAFETY line swap is now caught — closing today's hole where 26 Blake and 44 Alex Chinese constraint lines sit outside the count.

rows.title: EPIC-20260816 framework health repair (installer P0 data-deletion fixes)
rows.summary: Epic stood up after the 2026-08-16 full-repo audit (F-01~F-34 + S-01~S-04); hard constraint: no release and no install-command recommendations until Phase 2 passes Gate 4; F-15 direction and playground retirement still need human rulings before the Phase 1 handoff.
rows.cost_rationale: 36 audit findings across installer, tests and docs; the release ban makes this Epic-scale, multi-phase work.
rows.value_rationale: The installer currently deletes user data on every run; shipping it harms every downstream installer, so this is the highest-value safety fix in the backlog.
rows.deliverable: EPIC-20260816-framework-health-repair advanced through its phases: F-01 installer P0s (irreversible deletion of user .codex/, .gemini/, AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md and first-install CLAUDE.md overwrite) fixed in the same batch as F-34 (upgrade-acceptance.sh Check 3 no longer asserts those deletions as expected), with Gate 4 PASS before any release or install recommendation.

rows.title: Knowledge Staleness-Trap Sweeper for Principles and Patterns
rows.summary: The r4 research round identified a 'Staleness Trap' in persistent documents and OBJECTIVES lists it as residue, but nothing mechanically detects stale principles/patterns before agents act on them.
rows.cost_rationale: One checker script plus one report format across the knowledge tree; moderate scope, no new abstraction beyond the checker.
rows.value_rationale: Advances O3/KR2 (the persistent asset stays trustworthy, not just queryable) and O1/KR3 by closing the named residue Staleness Trap gap.
rows.deliverable: .tad/hooks/lib/staleness-check.sh (or .tad/scripts equivalent) that emits a staleness report listing every principles.md and patterns/*.md entry with last-verified age, whether files it references have changed since, and a current/stale verdict; acceptance: it runs clean on the TAD repo and correctly flags the known r4 staleness-trap cases documented in .tad/evidence/research/2026-07-staleness-trap-findings.md.

rows.title: AI/Human Capability-Boundary Awareness — Rubber Stamp Effect
rows.summary: Build capability-boundary awareness into agents: AI judges reasoning quality, humans judge direction/perception/taste; stop asking humans to rubber-stamp AI reasoning.
rows.cost_rationale: Scope is large and cross-cutting: principles wording, Gate 4 question redesign, and per-project adaptation.
rows.value_rationale: Gate 4 rubber-stamping silently defeats TAD's core quality claim; fixing the human环节 lifts every project.
rows.deliverable: Gate 4 redesigned so humans are asked only human-domain questions (direction, experience, taste shortlists instead of 'did Blake do it right'), with the capability-boundary rule written into principles.md and Alex/Blake SKILL.md.

rows.title: gen-floor.py: implement a real --check dry-run mode
rows.summary: Split-out small ticket (c) from the voided English-unification plan: gen-floor.py currently ignores its arguments entirely, so --check is silently swallowed and the script writes files anyway.
rows.cost_rationale: Single script, single flag, one no-write test; the smallest item in this backlog.
rows.value_rationale: A dry-run flag that secretly writes is a footgun in the floor-table workflow that the English-unification post-mortem already tripped over.
rows.deliverable: gen-floor.py actually parses arguments and implements --check as a true dry run that writes no files, proven by a test that runs it against a dirty tree and asserts file mtimes/contents are unchanged.

rows.title: TAD Self-Test Agent — Automated Agent Behavior Verification
rows.summary: Automated regression verification for TAD itself, replacing slow manual terminal checks after upgrades and syncs.
rows.cost_rationale: Requires a new test agent, check scripts, and a report format across several .tad components.
rows.value_rationale: Repeatable regression checks would catch broken skills, hooks, and configs before downstream projects inherit them.
rows.deliverable: A .tad/tests/ self-test agent that spawns a sub-agent, verifies config integrity, SessionStart hook output, /alex startup, and Domain Pack loading, and emits a PASS/FAIL report.

rows.title: Handoff volume gate: warn above 80KB / 20 AC before reviewers spawn
rows.summary: Measured distribution: the one handoff that blew up was 107KB/27AC; 64/62/52KB ones completed; the rest are <40KB. The warning must land before reviewers spawn, otherwise 'keep as-is' is the only rational choice.
rows.cost_rationale: One insertion point in the handoff flow plus a fixture test; moderate, well-bounded change.
rows.value_rationale: Oversized handoffs are the observed precursor to failed, expensive review chains; an early warning is cheap insurance.
rows.deliverable: A generation-time warning (prompt, not hard reject) fired when a handoff exceeds 80KB or 20 AC, inserted between step1b and step1c — before any reviewer is spawned — demonstrated with the 107KB/27AC shape as a fixture and a normal <40KB handoff passing silently.

rows.title: Production Observation Practice — Traces Hour for TAD-Designed Agents
rows.summary: PostHog Traces Hour: weekly human review of real production agent traces finds failure classes automated evals miss; TAD currently ends at delivery.
rows.cost_rationale: A new methodology module and recurring practice template; no new infrastructure.
rows.value_rationale: Fills a named gap in the TAD lifecycle that every agent-product user will hit immediately after launch.
rows.deliverable: A production-observation module (capability pack or TAD lifecycle extension) defining what to watch, a weekly Traces Hour template, and the feedback path from observed failures back into handoffs, extending the lifecycle to delivery, observe, improve, redesign.

rows.title: TAD Unified Auth Layer (tad auth)
rows.summary: Unified authentication status layer over TAD's 4+ heterogeneously-authenticated tools, with expiry pre-warning at agent startup.
rows.cost_rationale: Medium build for the status layer, but credential migration to keyring and per-tool quirks push it to safety-adjacent large.
rows.value_rationale: Login failures are a repeated, measured pain point; one early-warning check removes most surprise expiries.
rows.deliverable: A `tad auth status` command printing one unified table for gh, codex, gemini, and NotebookLM, auto-run at Alex/Blake startup, plus the fixed NotebookLM `Aborted!` false alarm and a unified auth-check verdict.

rows.title: Audit: Alex references mandatory lines survive by duplication, not loading
rows.summary: 82 of 83 mandatory lines in alex/references/** have no duplicate in the resident layer — today discipline holds by duplication, not by the loading mechanism; 8 of 9 forbidden lines are safe only by a lucky CLAUDE.md duplicate.
rows.cost_rationale: Reading and mapping work across the references tree plus a written audit; no behaviour change proposed by the audit itself.
rows.value_rationale: Knowing exactly which forbidden lines are one edit away from going dark is prerequisite to trusting the lightening work.
rows.deliverable: An audit report under .tad/evidence/ mapping all 83 mandatory lines in alex/references/** to whether each has a resident-layer duplicate, listing the 82 unduplicated lines and flagging which of the 9 forbidden lines lack a CLAUDE.md duplicate.

rows.title: yolo2 Phase 1 P2/LOW hardening tail (code, architecture, security)
rows.summary: Gate 3 PASS non-blocking follow-ups from yolo2 Phase 1 code/architecture/security reviews at fc7a07fc, recorded so they are not lost; pick items individually, do not bundle blindly.
rows.cost_rationale: A dozen-plus small fixes across code, architecture and security reviewers' lists, spanning many files and fixtures.
rows.value_rationale: Closes known robustness and low-severity security debt in the yolo2 ledger/reconcile path before it hardens into production behaviour.
rows.deliverable: Patches closing the listed OPEN items (fsync gaps, duplicated reason/exit-code table, reducer check order, errorResult schema, bare path.resolve in reconcile, missing --rebuild-derived in handoff §4.2, fixture gaps T-2/T-3/T-4, git-clean warning in guide §8, error branch in §4 new-session prompt) with the yolo2 test suite passing.

rows.title: TAD Repositioning — Judgment Surfaces for Domains Without Automatic Evaluators
rows.summary: Converged repositioning: TAD as a human-AI OS for domains with no automatic evaluator; its highest-value move is building judgment interfaces that compile human taste into structured,沉淀 data.
rows.cost_rationale: The converged next step is a single methodology write-up plus template, not the deferred README rewrite.
rows.value_rationale: Evidence-backed and already fossil-proven in two domains; it sharpens where TAD's marginal value is highest.
rows.deliverable: A judgment-surface guide in the core methodology layer: the reflex rule (no automatic evaluator + about to ask 'what do you think' -> build a judgment interface first) plus worked fossil examples from the podcast and playground HTML interfaces, with votes captured as structured data.

rows.title: Deprecate Domain Pack YAML Format
rows.summary: Retire the transitional Domain Pack YAML format in favor of Capability Packs, which agents follow as recipes rather than ingredient lists.
rows.cost_rationale: Large migration touching 12 remaining YAML packs, keyword routing, and four dependent backlog ideas.
rows.value_rationale: Removes a superseded dual format and the maintenance burden of keeping YAML criteria in sync with packs.
rows.deliverable: All 20 Domain Pack YAMLs retired: the 12 un-rebuilt packs either rebuilt as Capability Pack SKILL.md + references or archived with a decision record, and keywords.yaml routing replaced by SKILL.md frontmatter triggers.

rows.title: Transplant lite's unconditional round cap to the full channel
rows.summary: Lite has an unconditional repair_round 3/3 cap plus cross-compaction persistence; full only has error-shaped consecutive_same_error>=3, which resets forever when errors never repeat — a loop with ever-changing errors never stops.
rows.cost_rationale: Circuit-breaker design has already burned four Gate 2 rounds; expect Epic-phase scale work even with lite's answer in hand.
rows.value_rationale: An unbounded repair loop in the default full channel is a runaway-cost and runaway-edit risk on every long chain.
rows.deliverable: Full channel gains an unconditional repair-round cap with cross-compaction persistence, built on lite's boundary-append insight (stage-boundary enumeration, success-independent) rather than the bare '3 rounds' number, proven by a test where three differently-shaped errors in one phase trigger the stop; design must first re-read blocked HANDOFF-20260804-gate-loop-circuit-breaker.md (4 Gate 2 rounds, 26 P0, zero delivery).

rows.title: Deterministic Rules Over LLM Classification in Bounded Scenarios
rows.summary: Daria's Desk evidence: ~200 lines of rules beat LLM classification where patterns are clear; reserve LLM for the ambiguous residue.
rows.cost_rationale: Small, bounded replacement of one classification path plus a misclassification feedback loop.
rows.value_rationale: Faster, cheaper, and more predictable routing for the clear majority of intents.
rows.deliverable: Intent routing for the deterministic cases implemented as regex/keyword rules with a user learning filter for false positives, benchmarked against the current LLM router on accuracy and latency.

rows.title: Self-Evolving System — Domain Pack + Agent Auto-Optimization from Execution History
rows.summary: Trace-driven self-optimization of Domain Packs and agents: record traces, aggregate failure modes, propose criteria and step updates through Gates.
rows.cost_rationale: Large multi-stage system: trace capture, failure aggregation, and step-rewrite evaluation across the framework.
rows.value_rationale: Harness optimization has outsized leverage (Meta-Harness evidence), and traces are the missing data foundation for all later stages.
rows.deliverable: Stage 1 shipped: execution traces recorded as .tad/evidence/domain-traces/{domain}/{date}.jsonl (step ID, tool calls, duration, success/failure, failure reason) for every Domain Pack run.

rows.title: Resolve the express-review minimum contradiction (min 2 vs min 1)
rows.summary: Five places state express review minimum 2 while principles.md's SAFETY entry and AR-001 allow express to drop to min 1; P7 wrote the stricter min-2 side into a resident imperative, making the contradiction more visible; needs a human ruling.
rows.cost_rationale: Few files, but the ruling changes review strictness, so the edit is small and the deliberation is the cost.
rows.value_rationale: Contradictory review minimums in SAFETY text mean reviewers can legitimately cite either number, weakening the review floor.
rows.deliverable: A recorded human ruling on express-review minimum (1 vs 2), followed by harmonising all six locations (CLAUDE.md:63, alex/SKILL.md three sites, config-quality.yaml:74, principles.md SAFETY entry / AR-001) to the ruled value with grep proof of zero remaining contradictions.

rows.title: Domain Pack Monthly Refresh — Tools & Skills Periodic Update
rows.summary: Monthly refresh of tools-registry.yaml and domain skill research so packs do not silently go stale.
rows.cost_rationale: Small recurring template plus registry checks; no new abstraction required.
rows.value_rationale: Keeps tool recommendations current as new MCP servers and CLIs appear, at low recurring cost.
rows.deliverable: A monthly Domain Pack Health Check handoff template (or *maintain extension) that produces an updated tools-registry.yaml plus a changelog of replaced or new tools.

rows.title: SessionStart Full Component Health Check
rows.summary: Extend Alex/Blake startup checks from document health to full framework-component integrity, OpenHarness RuntimeBundle style.
rows.cost_rationale: One SessionStart hook extension plus a component checklist script.
rows.value_rationale: Catches missing hooks and version drift at startup instead of mid-task, where they currently surface as confusing failures.
rows.deliverable: A SessionStart health-check script that verifies hook scripts exist, config versions match, and template files are intact, warning or blocking at startup with a named list of broken components.

rows.title: Cheap Deterministic Loop + Expensive LLM Hybrid Architecture
rows.summary: Petri pattern: cheap deterministic inner loop runs continuously, expensive LLM intervenes only at key nodes, with deterministic fallback.
rows.cost_rationale: Convert a bounded set of startup checks to scripts and wire anomaly-only LLM escalation.
rows.value_rationale: Directly reduces per-session activation overhead, which is paid on every TAD session.
rows.deliverable: Startup activation checks (file age, grep-based state checks) implemented as deterministic bash scripts, with the LLM invoked only on anomalies, and a before/after measurement of activation token overhead.

rows.title: AC-08 baseline design knife: state boundary and complete-diff reporting
rows.summary: BACKLOG item named by GM, ticket not yet opened: ordinary PM, wrapper and trace writes break an ignored-byte baseline and AC-08 stops at the first mismatch, hiding the full diff.
rows.cost_rationale: Design-only knife spanning several state classes and the AC-08 checker, so moderate multi-file work.
rows.value_rationale: Stops recurring false AC-08 failures that block otherwise sound chains and misdirect debugging to the first mismatch only.
rows.deliverable: A design ticket/handoff in .tad/active/ defining the stable-source vs task-artifact vs external-owner vs runtime-output boundary, plus an AC-08 change that reports the complete diff set instead of stopping at the first mismatch, verified on a fixture with multiple mismatches.

rows.title: Hook Timeout Configuration
rows.summary: Add per-hook-type timeouts so a hung hook script cannot block TAD indefinitely.
rows.cost_rationale: Single settings change if Claude Code hooks lack native timeouts; verification step dominates.
rows.value_rationale: Cheap insurance against a whole class of silent hangs in every session.
rows.deliverable: timeout_seconds fields added to hook definitions in settings.json (30s command/http/prompt, 60s agent) with a test showing a hanging hook is cut off with a warning instead of blocking forever.

rows.title: Self-Critique Generation Pipeline + Transcript Mining
rows.summary: Generate, self-critique, filter, keep only合格 output — plus mining session transcripts for user-specific error patterns that personalize the system.
rows.cost_rationale: One pipeline applied to an existing generation flow, plus transcript-mining analysis over session records.
rows.value_rationale: Systematizes quality control TAD already does ad hoc in research verification and expert review.
rows.deliverable: A batch generation pipeline (applied first to skill drafts) that generates N candidates, self-critiques and filters them, and ships only passing ones, with the keep ratio and filter criteria logged.

rows.title: Capability Builder v1 Phase 4 — Voice Studio Dogfood (eval-page-generator)
rows.summary: Parked Phase 4 of Capability Builder v1: run the complete Create/Evolve/Package workflow in Voice Studio to materialize eval-page-generator from its accepted SCAND. Phases 1-3 are Gate 4 accepted; only Phase 4 remains, explicitly parked pending human resumption in Voice Studio.
rows.cost_rationale: This is a full Epic phase spanning skill creation, projection, WITH/CONTROL proof, evolution and plugin packaging in another project.
rows.value_rationale: Provides the only real-project end-to-end proof that the accepted Builder workflow works outside TAD fixtures, but Voice Studio is not a current priority project.
rows.deliverable: Voice Studio-owned eval-page-generator Skill at voice-studio/.agents/skills/eval-page-generator/SKILL.md that validates and is byte-identical to its .claude projection, with passing WITH-Skill vs failing CONTROL fixture evidence and a validated isolated Plugin wrapper under voice-studio/plugins/eval-page-generator/

rows.title: Re-audit lightening net savings: externalised-but-always-read items
rows.summary: The lightening ledger overstates savings: knowledge-bootstrap is read on every activation, only moved out of the measurement denominator, so the claimed net saving must be discounted ~25% and all similar externalisations rechecked by the same rule.
rows.cost_rationale: Re-measurement and arithmetic correction across the externalised items; single-digit files.
rows.value_rationale: Decisions about further lightening are being made against inflated savings numbers; correcting the ledger prevents chasing phantom gains.
rows.deliverable: A re-audit note correcting the lightening savings ledger: every externalised item whose load_when is 'every activation' (knowledge-bootstrap: 1,342B claimed inside a false 5,389B net saving) re-counted as still-read, with the headline net-saving figure revised down by the stated ~25%.

rows.title: Saveable Skills from Conversation Workflows
rows.summary: Linear Agent pattern: save a good conversational workflow as a reusable skill in one click, instead of TAD's ceremony-heavy Gate-KA-SCAND-harvest path.
rows.cost_rationale: Detection of reusable patterns in conversation plus a save/apply mechanism across existing skillify stages.
rows.value_rationale: More skills captured at the moment of value means the compounding corpus grows faster with less friction.
rows.deliverable: A *discuss/*bug-time prompt that detects when a conversation produced a reusable workflow and offers one-click saving into the skill library, bypassing the full Gate 4 KA ceremony for that path.

rows.title: State-Machine-Driven + Multi-Stream Sync Interaction Architecture
rows.summary: Simer pattern: make TAD's implicit protocol state machine explicit and give Gate reviews structured scorecards instead of free text.
rows.cost_rationale: Formalizing existing implicit protocol states across Alex/Blake plus a scorecard template.
rows.value_rationale: Explicit states improve reliability and debuggability of a flow that already exists implicitly.
rows.deliverable: An explicit state-machine specification for Alex/Blake protocol steps (states, entry/exit conditions, allowed actions per state) and a standardized Gate review scorecard template replacing free-text verdicts.

rows.title: Privacy: cross-repo trace entries still record absolute paths (AC12 residual)
rows.summary: AC12 residual: git rev-parse --show-toplevel is evaluated by cwd, not by file path, so traces of cross-repo writes still leak absolute downstream paths; semantics are ambiguous and may mean cross-repo writes should not be traced here at all.
rows.cost_rationale: Needs an independent design decision first, then a hook change plus cross-repo test fixtures.
rows.value_rationale: Absolute home paths in a shareable trace are a standing privacy leak, the same class the completed 0d item fixed for the single-repo case.
rows.deliverable: A design decision record plus trace-hook fix so cross-repo writes (e.g. *sync writing ~14 downstream projects) no longer record downstream repos' absolute /Users/<user>/ paths in this repo's trace, verified by a cross-repo write fixture, closing the AC12 residual from HANDOFF-20260816-trace-relative-path.md §7.1.

rows.title: Residual: experiment-path-protocol still auto-dumps the ai-evaluation SKILL
rows.summary: Residual carried from the completed pack-loader section: one protocol still force-loads a full skill body, the exact pattern the rest of the loader work eliminated.
rows.cost_rationale: Single loader behaviour in one protocol file plus a load test.
rows.value_rationale: Every forced full-skill dump is activation cost paid for content the task usually does not need.
rows.deliverable: experiment-path-protocol.md's capability_pack_auto_load changed so it no longer dumps the full ai-evaluation SKILL into context (thin/on-demand loading consistent with the completed pack-loader item), verified by a load trace showing the skill body absent until explicitly requested.

rows.title: TAD as Opt-In Mode (CLAUDE.md Posture Flip)
rows.summary: Flip TAD from ambient constitution to opt-in mode; PARKED because loosening the default might erode strictness inside explicitly invoked Alex/Blake mode.
rows.cost_rationale: Parked pending one experiment, but any CLAUDE.md posture change is framework-wide and safety-adjacent.
rows.value_rationale: Would cut posture overhead in casual use, but the user explicitly parked it until strictness-under-loose-default is guaranteed.
rows.deliverable: An experiment report answering the blocking question: after a loose ambient default, an explicit /alex invocation reloading the full SKILL.md is measured for strictness drift across repeated trials; only with a PASS does the CLAUDE.md opt-in posture flip proceed.

rows.title: Capability Builder P2 leftovers: stale-lock, hash overhead, timeout, awk hygiene
rows.summary: Leftover P2 items carried out of the completed Capability Builder Phase 2+3 section (the knowledge-distillation application was separately deferred to knowledge-maintain and the Voice Studio dogfood is human-started, so both are excluded here).
rows.cost_rationale: Four small, independent fixes from a closed phase; each is minor but they span different subsystems.
rows.value_rationale: Small reliability debts in a shipped capability; worth clearing opportunistically, not urgent.
rows.deliverable: The four remaining Capability Builder P2 items closed with tests: stale-lock recovery, large-tree hash overhead reduction, timeout-path cross-machine verification, and awk -- hygiene — each evidenced in a completion note under .tad/evidence/.

rows.title: JAX vmap Extreme Parallelism for Self-Play Training
rows.summary: Jaxpot pattern: vmap thousands of game environments on a single GPU for AlphaZero-style self-play, directly relevant to the Pokemon TCG AI project.
rows.cost_rationale: Feasibility hinges on rewriting a complex imperfect-information TCG environment in JAX, which may not vectorize cleanly.
rows.value_rationale: Could be a step-change in training speed for an active project if the environment ports to JAX.
rows.deliverable: A benchmark report: a JAX vmap prototype running parallel Pokemon TCG self-play environments on one GPU, measured in steps/second against the current self_play.py baseline, with a go/no-go recommendation.

rows.title: DeerFlow Patterns — Sandbox Isolation + Persistent Memory + Message Gateway
rows.summary: Borrow DeerFlow patterns TAD lacks: sandbox isolation, persistent cross-session memory, and a message gateway.
rows.cost_rationale: Three separate patterns (sandbox, memory, gateway) with no chosen first slice; container isolation alone is a large build.
rows.value_rationale: Safer execution of untrusted code is valuable, but the file bundles three unrelated patterns with no prioritized design.
rows.deliverable: A working sandbox-isolation prototype for Blake executing untrusted code (local/Docker tier) with a pass/fail run report comparing it to the current OS-level sandbox.

rows.title: config-cognitive reachability: two disciplines still invisible to Alex
rows.summary: Two disciplines (research first, technical decision transparency) still live only in config-cognitive.yaml, which Alex's STEP 3 never loads; resident imperative one-liners provide a fallback, so priority is lower than the fatal-operations move, and the bodies must be measured before paying +N bytes.
rows.cost_rationale: Measurement first, then at most one file move; small if the bodies turn out to carry little.
rows.value_rationale: Dark disciplines are unenforceable disciplines, but the existing one-line fallbacks cap the marginal gain.
rows.deliverable: A measurement note in .tad/evidence/ stating what the 'research first' and 'technical decision transparency' bodies in config-cognitive.yaml actually carry and their byte cost, followed — if judged worth it — by their relocation into a file Alex's STEP 3 actually loads, with parity checks green.

rows.title: Config Environment Variable Override
rows.summary: Add environment-variable override layer to TAD config, following OpenHarness's four-layer precedence.
rows.cost_rationale: Medium change to config loading logic plus documentation and naming-convention decisions.
rows.value_rationale: Standard for CI/container deployments, but the file itself notes TAD is currently mainly local CLI with no confirmed CI scenario.
rows.deliverable: Config loader supporting env-var overrides with documented precedence (default, file, env, CLI) and a test showing an env var overrides the YAML value.

rows.title: Optional: make Gate 3 verdicts machine-readable (unified wording or frontmatter)
rows.summary: Optional, explicitly not a defect: 10 of the last 20 COMPLETIONs carry Gate 3 verdicts in equivalent but non-template wording that machines cannot read; unifying wording or forcing frontmatter trades expressiveness for machine-readability and needs a human ruling before any ticket.
rows.cost_rationale: Wording standardisation touches many report templates and habits; cheap to spec, costly to enforce.
rows.value_rationale: Machine-readable verdicts would let checks stop warning 'cannot read' on 10 otherwise sound reports, but the payoff is convenience, not correctness.
rows.deliverable: A recorded human design ruling plus, if ruled in favour, a unified Gate 3 verdict frontmatter field (gate3_verdict:) added to the COMPLETION template with Check 8 reading it, demonstrated on one real completion file.

rows.title: Single-Loop Agent Without LangChain/LangGraph
rows.summary: PostHog AI rejected LangChain/LangGraph for direct API calls plus a single loop and dual-model strategy; evaluate the same for TAD-designed embedded agents.
rows.cost_rationale: An evaluation plus prototype loop, with the payoff depending on product-embedded-agent plans that are not yet active.
rows.value_rationale: Useful guidance for future embedded agents, but TAD's current orchestration need is already served.
rows.deliverable: A design evaluation with a working single-loop + mode-switch-tool prototype for one product surface, comparing controllability and cost against the framework-based orchestration, with a stated complexity ceiling.

rows.title: Imitation Learning + Classical AI Cross-Domain Bridge Pattern
rows.summary: Cross-domain bridge pattern: classical AI does provable planning, imitation learning does physical perception-action, a bridge layer connects them.
rows.cost_rationale: Single design note, but its payoff is diffuse and hard to verify.
rows.value_rationale: Reinforces an existing TAD design philosophy rather than adding a new capability.
rows.deliverable: A patterns entry documenting the bridge rule (deterministic systems keep search/planning/optimization; learned/LLM systems keep perception/judgment under uncertainty) with the LeRobot, petri, and Daria's Desk cases as worked examples.

rows.title: CRDT + Agent Safe-Boundary Hot-Swap Realtime Collaboration
rows.summary: Jam pattern: CRDT real-time collaboration plus agent hot-swap only at safe boundaries, mapping naturally onto TAD Gates as safe switch points.
rows.cost_rationale: A CRDT editing prototype is a new subsystem with no current multi-agent file-editing demand beyond worktrees.
rows.value_rationale: The safe-boundary insight is already embodied in Gates; the CRDT half solves a problem TAD does not currently have.
rows.deliverable: A prototype demonstrating two agents editing one file via Yjs CRDT with changes applied only at a Gate-defined safe boundary, plus a verdict on whether it beats worktree isolation.

rows.title: WebRTC as Agent + ML Model Lightweight Transport Layer
rows.summary: WebRTC as a lightweight, browser-native, low-latency transport layer for agent plus pluggable ML-model visual perception.
rows.cost_rationale: A working realtime video-plus-ML pipeline is a substantial prototype for a scenario TAD has not entered.
rows.value_rationale: Only relevant if TAD expands to non-developer visual-assistance scenarios, which is speculative.
rows.deliverable: A LiveKit WebRTC prototype piping a video stream through one pluggable ML model (detection or segmentation) to an LLM agent response, with measured end-to-end latency.

rows.title: Claude Code Automated Reverse Engineering + Game Data Pipeline
rows.summary: Originlab case: Claude Code automating reverse engineering (memory hunting, hooking, capture) and a game-data-to-training-data pipeline blueprint.
rows.cost_rationale: Large, open-ended research with unclear human-guidance needs and unresolved data-rights questions.
rows.value_rationale: Expands the known capability boundary, but no current TAD project needs legacy binary work.
rows.deliverable: A research notebook evaluating Claude-Code-automated reverse engineering on one bounded legacy/protocol target, documenting the automation boundary (steps automated vs human-guided) and data-rights constraints.
